Voat's new censorship

Downvoating is what reddit uses to silence dissenting views.

People don't typically upvoat, even if they like something. They will just look at it.

But when people get butthurt or see things they don't like they DO DOWNVOAT. You're assuming that people use both buttons the same way.

Voating is a censorship tool because it doesn't depend on rational argumentation. It only depends on CONSENSUS. That's why SRS use downvoat brigades because they know it's only purpose is to censor content they don't want seen by others.

Look, our entire political system should make it more practical. We don't let everyone vote in elections for a good reason: we know that retards are the majority of people. You want Bill Gate's educated vote negated by some homeless retard on the street? That's EXACTLY what democratic voting does. That's exactly what the movie Idiocracy was about. When you give everyone an equal say, you negate the point of education. You negate the point of rational argumentation. If a baby can negate the vote of an adult, then you don't really need to learn how to think. All you need to do is make people agree with you. And bribery is the fastest way to agreement.

Since people tend to downvoat when they're butthurt and engaged in censorship, the best way to combat censorship would be to only allow UPVOATING since people will actively have to champion what they believe rather than focus on what they want to complain about and censor. You can look at upvoating as positive censorship since it at least puts the burden on the upvoater to be accountable to their views and say what they prefer instead of simply complaining about what they don't want.

Stating what you want to happen takes EDUCATION AND EFFORT. Complaining about what you don't want just requires the ability to be butthurt.

I'd rather err on the side of positive censorship if we have to censor at all. We already know how negative censorship turns out: it becomes reddit.

At least positive censorship requires EFFORT that keyboard warriors aren't willing to invest. So if we want to make this place different from reddit, we should ONLY have an upvoat button.

And while we're at it, let's remove the scores from the profiles so keyboard warriors who are already socially retarded don't start jerking off to their fake internet power.

Ok so I was reading an article and it states

"In the most recent Fox News poll (note to those who are anti-Fox: Fox News polls are conducted by an independent, bipartisan organization)..."

So that got me thinking, where do any of these polls come from and how accurate could the be? I mean, I have never done one neither has anyone Ive talked to, so where do they get the data?

for a few years i was polled by one of the big polling companies (can't remember which one now) they would call every month or two and ask a ton of questions and then cut me a check. it was fun and the extra money was nice.

There's a few, but the short of it is that people on the news organization's payroll ask people individually how they feel on an issue.

In Fox News' case, they outsource to two different companies that tend to lean conservative and liberal, respectively. That company then calls about a thousand people to ask their opinion on an issue. Usually, they're given the choices given in the poll. Smaller news organizations (maybe larger than a local paper, but smaller than Fox News) have the same idea, but do it in-house. A local newspaper might stand outside of an election polling center to get an opinion from folks, stand outside of a busy area in the city, call people in the area, or post a poll on their website.

Generally, the number of sources (people they interview/poll) is disclosed to keep things ethical. In terms of accuracy, it depends, because you're trusting people at their word — but I guess that's a question for any opinion polling (Gallup, etc).

I am planning on buying a shotgun for home defense. It will be my first shotgun purchase. Should I get a pump or semi-auto? What is the best for the price? I can spend up to $800. Thanks.
What should be my first shotgun?

Depends on what you are looking for. Do you have any shotgunning history at all or is this going to be the very first shotgun you've ever fired?

Feel, looks, functionality, durability, warranties, workmanship, and price are all worth thinking about. Not in that particular order, but all come into play.

Most people choose from the big four

Winchester Remington Mossberg Beretta

There are many, MANY other solid brands out there but I've noticed most first timers stick to these four. All four have a decent reputation for putting quality shotguns on the market for reasonable prices. There are so many 870 vs. 500 debates out there it can get a little old at times.

My suggestion, go to the local gun store. Even if that happens to be walmart. Start picking up the ones that look cool to you. I know this sounds silly but it usually works pretty well. Hold them up but try not to point them at the gun salesperson. It's considered bad manners. If you feel you must pull the trigger to see how it goes "click", ask them if you can. Once again, manners. Same for pumping the action if it's a pump.

Now after you've handled quite a few of them your going to start getting a feel for what you think you like. Go with your gut on this one. I hate when people find a gun they think they want but then get online. Here's a hint to every prospective gun buyer in the history of the internet. EVERY GUN will have negative reviews from what seems like a lot of people. The problem being, most of it's hearsay, and very few of these people have actually held said gun. They heard from some site that the grip on this gun is slippery so now it's what they're spewing on another site. It's ugly, and happens. Seriously, go ahead and try to find a firearm with 100% positive internet reviews.

Okay, rant over. Now that you have what you think you want in your mind try to find a range that does rentals. Odds are good they will have your potential firearm if it's one of the four. If not, ask your friends. I guarantee that if you have at least a dozen friends, one of them has a shotgun.

It's all about your personal preference. Nobody can tell you, "this is the bestest shotgun ever" and be correct. Most modern firearms are made pretty well. I had an old 'smith tell me once on this subject, "hold a bunch of em. The one that feels like your pecker in your hand is the one you want". ;) Good luck.
